headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Notion AI can expose workspace content while Replit Agent can read/write code and secrets, creating unsafe cross-workspace workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI is a workspace Q&A system over shared pages, and Replit Agent can read/write persistent Repl files. If users copy Notion-generated content into Replit prompts or files, attacker-controlled text can steer Replit. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, but the bridge is indirect rather than automatic.
conditions: IF Notion content is manually pasted into Replit prompts or files
IF Replit Agent treats pasted workspace text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy: paste only quoted excerpts, never raw instructions.
Add a visible delimiter around imported text and require the agent to ignore embedded commands.
Review any Notion-derived prompt before sending it to Replit.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between workspace notes and coding prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. Because Replit has broad network egress and secret handling, moving Notion content into Replit can expose sensitive workspace data beyond the original workspace boundary. The profiles do not show a built-in isolation layer between them.
conditions: IF workspace pages contain confidential business data
IF any Notion-derived text is copied into Replit files or prompts
IF Replit Agent sends that content to external services or deployments
mitigations: Do not paste confidential Notion pages into Replit.
Redact secrets and internal identifiers before transfer.
Use a separate sanitized summary document as the handoff artifact.
Check Replit logs and deployment outputs for leaked workspace text.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or content filtering on the handoff path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances, and Replit Agent has persistent Repl filesystem state with write access. If both are used on the same project artifacts, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or create inconsistent state. The conflict is plausible in default workflows, though not as severe as unrestricted shared git writes.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same exported notes, specs, or code files
IF changes are synchronized without locking or merge review
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each artifact.
Use timestamped exports instead of live shared editing.
Manually diff files before accepting changes.
Freeze one workspace copy during the other agent's edit session.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and Replit Agent acts inside a Repl with user checkpoints. If Notion outputs are treated as authoritative specs or facts and then fed into Replit for implementation, errors can cascade into code, deployments, or secret-handling changes. The pair lacks a documented verification gate.
conditions: IF Notion-generated summaries are used as implementation requirements
IF Replit Agent commits or deploys based on those summaries without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human review of Notion outputs before implementation.
Cross-check claims against source documents or code.
Use a checklist that separates summary, spec, and action steps.
Block direct deployment from unverified Notion-derived instructions.
requires-engineering: add automated verification between summarization and execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Replit Agent handles source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. If regulated data such as secrets or personal data is copied from Notion into Replit, the differing storage and retention contexts can create compliance mismatches. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than higher.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Notion pages and then transferred into Replit secrets or files
IF retention or deletion obligations differ between the two workspaces
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools when possible.
Store only references, not raw sensitive values, in either system.
Document which system is the system of record for each data class.
Review retention settings in both products before use.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows across tools.
